paragraphs: R' Yosi HaChorem (a Tanna of a baraita).
He is mentioned in [Menachot 37a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.37a.1-2). He said: We find that the right [hand] is called yad (hand), and Rabbi Natan says: It is not necessary, etc.

And in the [Mekhilta, Pischa 17](https://www.sefaria.org/Mekhilta_DeRabbi_Yishmael%2C_Tractate_Pischa.17.27), the statement is repeated, and there [it reads] Abba Yosi and R' Yonatan; Hyman says it should read R' Natan. In the book Sheerit Yaakov it is written (cited in [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1994&lang=en)) that what we find in Bekhorot 43a (compare [Bekhorot 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.43b.18)), ‘Rabbi Yosi says: Charum means only one who applies kohl to both his eyes,’ is [the statement of] R' Yosi HaChorem, and he was called this after that halakhah.

And Hyman suggests that this may be the intent of [Rashi on Menachot 37a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Menachot.37a.1.1), where he explains HaChorem as ‘his nose is sunken.’ For Hyman finds it very hard to say that because his nose was sunken they would call him by this derogatory name; rather, he says Rashi’s intent is that this R' Yosi stated the ruling ‘Charum means only one who applies kohl to both his eyes,’ namely, that his nose is sunken.[^1]

notes.text: [Hyman, vol. II, p. 740](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=323) gives Menachot 37a and Mekhilta Bo chapter 17. The supplied Hebrew transcribes 36a and chapter 7. In the consulted Mekhilta, Beeri’s Hebrew has Rabbi Natan and Abba Yoseh Hecharam, while Silverstein’s English gives Rabbi Yonathan and Abba Yossi. The Bekhorot locution “both eyes at once” is Rabbi Yosi’s wording there. Hyman treats the ruling as a possible explanation of the epithet.
